single_hypothesis: BUILD/CORRECTNESS FIX: only replace host sqrtf with Ascend C Sqrt, narrow DataCopyPad byte lengths to uint32_t, and preserve FP32 output values while retaining FP16/BF16 CAST_RINT; no performance mechanism.

build.command: bash ./build_server3.sh with ASC_DIR and CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH set to /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/8.5.0.alpha002/aarch64-linux/tikcpp/ascendc_kernel_cmake plus GCC 11 include/library paths

local_probes.kind: paired host numerical shim timing probes; no NPU kernel timing

device_timing.reason: Five server3 observations over about 20 seconds found VLLM/engine/python processes on all eight NPUs. Devices 0-3 stayed around 31-32 percent AICore, device 4 around 65 percent, devices 5-6 at 0 percent while occupied, and device 7 HBM stayed around 65192-65504/65536 MB. No comparable device-load window appeared, so neither side was executed for NPU timing.

local_probes.interpretation: Raw host-shim timings are recorded for paired inputs only. The load is contaminated and no device-performance or improvement conclusion is made.

load_quality.observation: During paired probes, existing VLLM/python processes remained on the NPUs. The recorded snapshots show HBM usage about 90-99 percent, AICore about 31-33 percent on devices 0-3 and 0 percent on devices 4-7; exact device and process output is in the paired probe log.
load_quality.note: No latency or performance claim is made.

main_review_self_audit.scope: The diff contains only the device sqrt API replacement, two uint32_t DataCopyPad length conversions, and the FP32 output copy while retaining FP16/BF16 CAST_RINT. No tile, buffer, queue, ownership, timing, or profiling mechanism was added.
